about: Labels the LLM uses to name its RTL edits (Transformations section of the answer) and the Vivado evidence that Analysis/EditLog.py checks for each label. 'description' is shown to the LLM and only says what the label means, never when to use it. 'evidence' is a list of alternatives; an alternative is a list of conditions that must ALL hold between the REFERENCE and the attempt; the label is 'confirmed' when ANY alternative holds. A condition is {'metric': key, 'change': c} or {'primitive': [name prefixes], 'change': c}, with c in up | down | not_up | not_down. 'strength' is 'direct' when the evidence is the primitive the label is about, and 'indirect' when it is only a metric trend that other edits could also explain. An empty evidence list means the label cannot be checked from the reports ('unverifiable').

MEM_TO_BRAM.description: A memory or register array is described so that Vivado maps it to block RAM (RAMB18E1/RAMB36E1).

MEM_TO_LUTRAM.description: A memory or register array is described so that Vivado maps it to distributed (LUT) RAM.

SRL_INFERENCE.description: A chain of registers without reset or intermediate taps is described so that Vivado maps it to a shift-register LUT (SRL16E/SRLC32E).

MULT_TO_DSP.description: A multiplication (or multiply-accumulate) is described so that Vivado maps it to a DSP48E1.

MULT_TO_LOGIC.description: A multiplication is kept out of the DSP48E1 blocks and built from LUTs and carry chains.

DSP_ABSORB_PIPE_REGS.description: Registers around a multiplication (input, multiplier or output registers) are described so that they are absorbed into the DSP48E1 (A/B, M, P registers) instead of fabric flip-flops.

DSP_USE_PREADDER.description: An addition before a multiplication is described so that it uses the pre-adder of the DSP48E1.

DSP_CASCADE.description: A sum of products is described so that partial sums travel over the dedicated cascade path between DSP48E1 blocks (PCIN/PCOUT).

FANOUT_REPLICATION.description: A register with a large fan-out is duplicated so that each copy drives fewer loads.

LOGIC_RETIME.description: Combinational logic is moved from one side of a register to the other to balance the logic depth between registers, without changing the register-crossing count at the outputs.

LOGIC_SIMPLIFICATION.description: An expression, comparator, mux or controller is rewritten with less logic (shared terms, narrower widths, simpler encoding).

RESOURCE_SHARING.description: One arithmetic unit or memory port is used for several operations (time multiplexing) instead of one unit per operation.

CONTROL_SET_REDUCTION.description: Resets, enables or clocks of registers are unified so that fewer distinct control sets exist.

OTHER.description: Any edit that fits none of the labels above; describe it in 'rationale'.
